name: Loyalino
summary: Shopify loyalty app from OkayScale: points on orders and actions, VIP tiers by points or spend, referrals with dual-sided rewards, shown in a floating widget, the cart, product pages, customer accounts, a standalone storefront page and Shopify POS. Runs in the EU, ships in eight languages. Launched June 2026, no reviews yet.
best_for: shopify stores whose loyalty orders sit comfortably below a plan ceiling and who want the whole program - points, VIP tiers, referrals, the widget, a customer-accounts loyalty page and eight built-in languages - on a free tier that withholds almost nothing, with the developer reachable directly rather than through a help centre
skip_if: your monthly order count swings or runs close to a plan ceiling: at the limit the program pauses for the rest of the calendar month instead of billing you overage. Skip it too if you need Shopify POS, the REST API or email from your own sending domain, because all three start at $29 a month - and if you want a loyalty app with a track record, because this one has no reviews at all
honest_knock: Reach your plan's order limit and the program does not cost more, it stops. Their FAQ is explicit about it: at a finite plan limit the loyalty program pauses until the next calendar month or an eligible upgrade, and there are no per-order overage fees. For most metered apps that would be a mercy. For a loyalty program it means points quietly stop accruing for your customers partway through your busiest month, which is exactly when you least want it, and the free plan's ceiling of 200 orders is reached by a store doing seven orders a day. The ladder pushes the same direction: on their published rates the price per loyalty order gets worse with every step up rather than better - about $0.058 an order at Starter's 500, $0.065 at Essential's 2,000 and $0.071 at Growth's 7,000, which is our arithmetic on their figures at each plan's ceiling. And the thing they sell hardest is the thing you cannot check from outside: one-to-one support on every plan including the free one, and custom development included on the paid ones, from the people who wrote the code. That is a real differentiator if it holds. The app launched on 16 June 2026 and carries no reviews at all, so nothing independent stands behind it yet.

pricing.notes: (prices read 22 September 2026 on apps.shopify.com/loyalino-loyalty-rewards and on loyalino.io/pricing) Billed in USD through Shopify and metered by monthly loyalty orders rather than by features. The vendor puts it in those words on its own pricing page - you pay for volume, not for features - and every paid plan carries the same paid feature set. Free: $0 for up to 200 loyalty orders a month. Starter: $29 a month or $290 a year for up to 500. Essential: $129 or $1,290 for up to 2,000. Growth: $499 or $4,990 for up to 7,000. Enterprise: $999 or $9,990 for unlimited orders with no cap. Annual billing works out at ten monthly payments, which is where the 17% they advertise comes from. Their FAQ defines a monthly loyalty order as one distinct Shopify order that creates a loyalty-points transaction in that calendar month, counted once however many transactions it generates. What the paid tiers add on top of the free plan is the standalone storefront loyalty page, earning and redemption in Shopify POS, sending from your own email domain, and the REST API, webhooks and MCP server. Points, the reward types, VIP tiers, referrals, the floating widget, the product-page and cart placements, the customer-accounts loyalty page, eight languages and eight loyalty emails are all on the free plan. Two terms to read before you count on the trial: a store gets up to 14 trial days, days used in the last 180 count against that, and a store billed for a Loyalino plan in the last 180 days gets no new trial at all. The 30-day money-back guarantee runs from the day your first paid plan activates, trial included, and upgrading, downgrading, renewing, cancelling or reinstalling does not restart that window. Asking for the refund does not cancel the subscription - that is a separate step.

compare_with.name: Essential Loyalty
compare_with.why: Both are Shopify loyalty apps that leave VIP tiers and referrals on the free plan and bill you by orders rather than by feature, so the comparison turns on what each one counts. Essential Loyalty meters loyalty-influenced orders; Loyalino counts any distinct order that creates a points transaction that month, which catches the customer who merely earns points on a purchase they were going to make anyway. Worth knowing before you read that as a verdict: neither vendor publishes how the other's definition behaves in practice, so check your own first full month against the counter rather than against the wording. Where Loyalino is clearly ahead is in what it tells you up front - the full ladder to $999, the cap behaviour, the trial arithmetic and EU data residency are all written down. Where it is clearly behind is evidence: zero reviews since launching in June 2026.

exit_test.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which we set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 17 November 2026 the session tested Loyalino on a Shopify development store: the install, the one-screen onboarding, one click that made a loyalty program live with 5 points per $1, the Program and Home pages, the plan page with the Starter test subscription approved without a card (billed 0 dollars) and the uninstall dialog, after which the app was uninstalled. No order was placed and nothing was saved in the theme; nothing was paid. Install: the App Store listing of Loyalino: Loyalty & Rewards by Appal.io (Esbjerg, Denmark; launched 16 June 2026, 0 reviews) says Free plan available. Free trial available. and lists the plans Free $0 (200 loyalty orders a month), Starter $29, Essential $129, Growth $499 and Optional Enterprise: $999/mo, with data access to Customers, products, orders, discounts, store credit, Online Store, custom data, Shopify admin. The install was approved at about 15:10 in the Install app dialog of the admin, and the app opened straight on Set up your program, a short onboarding with the preference 5% back (5 points per $1), the tiers Bronze, Silver, Gold and Platinum, Ways to earn (5) and Rewards (2: Free shipping at 500 points and a Flexible amount discount). Core action, a loyalty rule that gives points per purchase: one click on Build and go live. The message said Your loyalty program is live and Customers earn points on real orders from now on. You can pause it from the menu at the top of this page. Time, approximate tester observations: install at about 15:10 and the program live at about 15:11, so about 1 minute, in about 5 actions (open the listing, the install form, Install, the onboarding and Build and go live). The Program page then shows Points on orders: All products, On the subtotal, Not on gift cards, Points arrive when the order is paid, 5 points per $1. Ways to earn: Sign up for an account 250 points, Follow on Instagram 50, Follow on TikTok 50, Subscribe to our newsletter 100, and Celebrate a birthday and Daily store visit both Off. On the right is a preview, A member's page, with 0 points and Make a purchase at 5 points per $1. The Home page shows Where members see it: Customer account page On; Launcher, Points on products, Points in the cart and Loyalty page Off; Free plan with 0 of 200 orders this month; and Finish your setup at 2 of 5 (open: Set up tiers, Add the launcher and Build your loyalty page). No order was placed and no theme change was saved, so earning points in the shop was not seen. Plans: in Settings the entries Point of sale, API keys, Claude and other MCP clients and Webhooks carry a lock marked Starter plan on the Free plan. The Plan page says Development store: Select any plan and approve Shopify's test subscription. No real charge is made on this development store., shows 0 of 200 orders with 200 left that starts over on 1 December, and 14-day free trial on every paid plan. Starter $29 every 30 days, 500 orders; Essential $129, 2,000 orders (No per-order overage fees); Growth $499, 7,000 orders; Enterprise $999 with No limit on orders; Free $0 with 200 loyalty orders per month. Each paid plan says New test subscription, no charge; yearly is Yearly, 2 months free; at the bottom there are 30 days, money back with Ask for a refund. Deviation from the App Store: Enterprise at $999 is an ordinary plan on the Plan page and the App Store calls it Optional Enterprise; the rest agrees. Checkout: Starter was chosen and opened the Shopify Approve subscription screen: You will not be billed for this test charge., Loyalino: Loyalty & Rewards by Appal.io, plan Loyalino Starter (Monthly), $29,00 USD every 30 days, You have a 14-day free trial ending on 1 Dec., subtotal $29,00 plus any applicable taxes, total $29,00 due 1 Dec. An Add payment method row stood on the screen, but Approve was active and nothing had to be entered. Because the screen says it is a test charge, it was approved without a card; nothing was billed. The app then showed Starter, $29.00 USD every 30 days, development store, Trial ends 1 Dec 2026 (UTC) and 0 of 500 orders. No card or payment method was entered. Cancelling: the Plan page has a button Switch to Free (not clicked) and Ask for a refund (not clicked). The app was uninstalled via Settings, Apps and Uninstall; the dialog Uninstall Loyalino: Loyalty & Rewards? says you will no longer be able to use the app, that any data managed by the app, such as discounts, will be deleted, and that a request goes to the app developer within 48 hours to delete all personal customer information. A reason is required (we chose Testing multiple apps) and the feedback box was left empty; the message You have successfully uninstalled followed. Not tested: a real order and points in the shop, the launcher or widget in the theme editor, setting up the VIP tiers, referrals, Shopify POS (locked on Free and not opened after Starter), the API, MCP and webhooks, e-mails and the vendor chat. Clean up: the loyalty program was switched live in the app (the app made it from its own onboarding defaults) and no theme change was saved; the Starter test subscription was approved without a payment; the app was uninstalled, so the program and the subscription ended with it; all browser tabs were closed. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The program goes live in one click on the defaults of the onboarding, while only 2 of 5 setup steps are done and the launcher, points on products and points in the cart are Off; Point of sale, API keys, MCP clients and webhooks are locked on the Free plan; the Starter approval screen has an Add payment method row and says only that it is a test charge; and Enterprise is an ordinary plan on the plan page while the App Store calls it optional.

claim_checks.claim: Free plan available. Free trial available.
claim_checks.observed: The App Store says a free plan and a free trial exist; the Plan page shows Free at 0 of 200 orders and a 14-day free trial on every paid plan, and the program was made live on the Free plan without a card.
claim_checks.plan: Starter test subscription approved without a card, development store
claim_checks.comparability: App Store free plan wording versus the Free plan counter and the trial label on the Plan page.
claim_checks.buying_consequence: You can run a points program for up to 200 loyalty orders a month at no cost, and try a paid plan for 14 days.

claim_checks.observed: The Plan page shows Enterprise at $999 with No limit on orders as an ordinary plan next to Starter, Essential and Growth, while the App Store calls it optional.
claim_checks.plan: Starter test subscription approved without a card, development store
claim_checks.comparability: App Store wording for Enterprise versus its card on the Plan page.
claim_checks.buying_consequence: The top plan of $999 a month is shown as a normal plan in the app, not as an extra to ask for.

claim_checks.claim: Customers earn points on real orders from now on.
claim_checks.observed: The app says customers earn points on real orders after Build and go live; no order was placed and no launcher or points display was switched on in the shop, so no points were earned or seen.
claim_checks.plan: Starter test subscription approved without a card, development store
claim_checks.comparability: Message after going live versus a shop where no order was placed.
claim_checks.buying_consequence: The test says nothing about whether points are awarded correctly when an order is paid.

claim_checks.observed: About 1 minute after the install and in about 5 actions, one click on Build and go live made a program live with 5 points per $1 on All products, on the subtotal, not on gift cards; the member preview shows 0 points and Make a purchase at 5 points per $1.
claim_checks.plan: Starter test subscription approved without a card, development store
claim_checks.comparability: Onboarding promise of a program in minutes versus the Program page and the preview; the shop side was not seen.
claim_checks.buying_consequence: A basic points rule can be live within a minute, but only the rule and its preview were seen.

claim_checks.claim: 14-day free trial on every paid plan
claim_checks.observed: The Shopify approval screen for Starter says You have a 14-day free trial ending on 1 Dec., as the Plan page says for every paid plan; Starter was approved as a test charge without a card.
claim_checks.plan: Starter test subscription approved without a card, development store
claim_checks.comparability: Plan page trial wording versus the approval screen; the trial ended with the uninstall.
claim_checks.buying_consequence: A 14-day trial exists on the paid plans and starting it on a development store needs no card.

claim_checks.observed: The Essential card says No per-order overage fees and Predictable flat-rate pricing; only Starter was approved, so what happens above 500 orders on Starter was not seen and Essential was not started.
claim_checks.plan: Starter test subscription approved without a card, development store
claim_checks.comparability: Essential card wording versus a plan that was not started and no orders.
claim_checks.buying_consequence: The test says nothing about what a shop pays when it goes over the order limit of a plan.

claim_checks.observed: The Plan page ends with 30 days, money back and a button Ask for a refund; neither was clicked, since nothing was paid.
claim_checks.plan: Starter test subscription approved without a card, development store
claim_checks.comparability: Refund wording at the bottom of the Plan page versus a test charge that was never billed.
claim_checks.buying_consequence: The 30 day refund promise could not be tried because the test charge billed nothing.

claim_checks.observed: The Shopify approval screen for Starter shows $29,00 USD every 30 days, a total of $29,00 due 1 Dec. plus any applicable taxes, and the plan card says $29 every 30 days; Approve was active and the test charge was approved without a card.
claim_checks.plan: Starter test subscription approved without a card, development store
claim_checks.comparability: Plan card price versus the approval screen amount; no stored cost rule was compared.
claim_checks.buying_consequence: The price of $29 a month on the plan card matches the approval screen before taxes, after a trial of 14 days.
